Besides LSTD concentration, analysis 'relies on the contractiveness of stable policies' through the LQ plant (Lyapunov stability, mixing) to bound regret: L_dyn.

Doubt between tr and pop (expected cost over x0~D0); rule 6 picks smaller scope; guarantee concerns stability/convergence over closed-loop trajectories.

Concentration-of-measure upper bound on adversarial accuracy/distance for any classifier; no classes.csv class (GEN, PROB) covers impossibility bounds.

Review restating results proved elsewhere ("proof is in (25)"); headline is an approximation-existence theorem over function classes, not a guarantee about a learned component; generalization part conjectural/cited.
Theorem 1 bounds expected population risk (E over D and SGD) by OPT+eps; probability is over random initialization, not data distribution; E per codebook.
Lemma 5.1 carries surrogate policy regret to true trajectory cost via (kappa,gamma)-strong-stability contraction of the LDS plant model; matches L_dyn definition.

Exchangeability/consistency assumptions stated; held-out real-data tests (Table 1, Fig. 3) supply evidence of coverage, but no confidence level enters the guarantee.
Strongest evidence: empirical coverage measured on real-world CRSP stock-return and CPS wage data (Sec. 5), beyond the analytical theorems.

Sampling is the construction's own randomness (already Ac); no argument carries the bound to larger scope. Rule 3 concerns certificates checked by sampling, not applicable.
Bound is analytical (Thm 7/Cor 8); no certificate computed on actual pruned nets, which are fine-tuned afterwards; 'proof' requires certificate on actual model.
Learned component is a representation/feature extractor ("last layer of a CNN"), motivated by ImageNet classification; codebook maps classifiers to perception.
Invariance by construction (Thm 1-2) fits no classes.csv code; both coders agree on NEW, concise label chosen.
Safety guarantee rests on GP confidence bounds of unknown safety function (Lemma 1, Thm 1); LUC explicitly covers GP learned-uncertainty safe control.
Learned GP safety/reward maps feed value-iteration path planning on a grid MDP; not a learned state-to-action controller.
GP concentration bound (L_conc); Lipschitz g plus reachability/returnability through known transition f extend safety to all t (L_dyn); X- confinement is enforced, not ODD containment.
Regret bounds one learning run over horizon T from any initial distribution; rule 6: in doubt between tr and pop choose smaller scope.
Population adversarial risk is reached from n i.i.d. training samples via probabilistic convergence (w.p. tending to 1): a concentration argument from samples.
Headline is an analytic asymptotic theorem under Gaussian linear data model (4); simulations only illustrate it, so analytical model is the strongest evidence.
Process/measurement noise and inputs are i.i.d. Gaussian (unbounded); codebook 'disturbance' requires bounded additive term, so this is natural sampling variation.
Bounded quantity is the policy value gap, an expected discounted return (Theorem 1, Lemma 1); the 1-delta sample confidence is captured by the L_conc lift.
Noise xi, eta are i.i.d. Gaussian, not a bounded additive disturbance; the w.p. 1-delta bound ranges over sampling variation.
Coded guarantee is delta-safety: C-UCRL policy satisfies CMDP cost constraints at all steps during learning (Theorem 3), a safety certificate for RL, not merely regret.
Excluded: guarantee concerns regularized DeePC on Hankel data matrices of an LTI system; no learned (ML) component, power converter only.

(eps,delta)-DP proven analytically via moments accountant for all neighbouring datasets; no Monte Carlo certification, so not Ac (certifier's own sampling).
Guarantee bounds l_inf error of the estimated optimal Q-function (title: optimal value estimation); no closed-loop policy is certified.
Headline bound is analytical (Thm 2); the toy 2-state MDP check is an illustration, not a simulator or benchmark environment.
Data-driven Wasserstein ambiguity set learned from disturbance samples; closed-loop chance-constraint guarantee w.p. 1-beta; fits LUC (learned-uncertainty, chance-constrained control).
Thm 4.3 bounds L2(mu) error by optimisation duality gaps; no sampling, shift or threat model enters the bound.
Headline regret bounds are analytical (Thms 3.2-3.3); synthetic Gaussian experiments only illustrate, not a simulator or benchmark environment.
Headline coverage validated on real-world datasets (MIMIC, Insurance, COVID19, EEG, Load); codebook: measured means real-world data.
Perturbation is sim-to-real transition-kernel mismatch framed as DRO, not an additive state disturbance term; codebook: distribution covers natural sampling variation or shift.
Bound carries performance on n i.i.d. training samples to population expected risk (PAC-type rates for VC classes); this is a sample-based L_conc argument.
Controller is computed from data with an SDP Lyapunov/ROA/RPI certificate. It is not neural (NCERT), not NN reachability (CLR), and not GP/chance-constrained (LUC).
Regret bound holds over stochastic transitions of an unknown MDP sampled during learning; the codebook calls this natural sampling variation (distribution), not none.
Bound on data-based simulation/output-matching error; not safe control, so LUC (learned-uncertainty safe control) does not fit any listed class.

Coverage/CI experiments include real-world data (Stanford HIV drug resistance, LIBSVM bodyfat); measured means real-world data, the strongest class present.
